sentences.text: 1. On the allegations of one Ms. Laxmi, PS Ambedkar Nagar registered an FIR and after concluding the investigation, filed a charge-sheet for offences punishable under Sections 498/406/354/34 IPC,
the Ld. Trial Court took cognizance of those offences and summoned the accused persons.

Subsequently, arguments on charge were heard and on 30.07.2019, the Ld. Trial Court passed an order opining that certain offences were made out against the accused persons and adjourned the matter for framing of charge.
On the adjourned dated I.e 22.08.2019, the Ld. Trial Court framed the charge.

Aggrieved by this order dated 22.08.2019 Udit Bedi and Meena filed the revision No.
365/19, Rajan Gogoi filed the revision no. 364/19 and three other accused persons namely, Gayatri Devi, Komal Bedi and Navjot bedi filed criminal revision no. 361/19.
All the three revision petitions have come to this court upon transfer and now all the three revision petitions shall be disposed of by this common judgment.

sentences.text: 2. Both the sides have been heard.
Record perused.
3. The Ld. Trial Court in her order dated 30.07.2019 has given detailed reasons to arrive at her conclusion about prima facie satisfaction in respect of the offences.
The reason so given are re-produced as under:-
1. The matter is listed for orders on the aspect of charge.

2. It was inter-alia the submissio of Ld. Counsel for the accused persons that the allegations made against all the accused persons except the accused persons i.e.
husband and mother in law of the complainant were vague in nature and no case U/s 498 A IPC was disclosed against any of them.

3. Ld. APP for the State on the other hand submitted that prima facie case made out against all the accused persons and the offence U/s 4 Dowry Prohibition Act was also disclosed against the accused persons.
4. I have heard the arguments and perused the record.
5. It is well settled law that at the stage of framing of charge it only has to be seen whether a prima facie case is made out and the defence of the accused is not to be gone into.

6. In the original complaint, the complainant has made allegations against the accused persons Udit Bedi, Rajan Gogoi, Navjot Bedi, Gayatari Bedi and Kunal Bedi of subjecting her to cruelty including harassment for dowry.
The complainant has also made allegations against the accused Rajan Gogoi regarding outraging her modesty and sexually harassing her on atleast two occasions i.e. 28.06.2017 and 04.07.2017.
These allegations have been reiterated by the complainant in her statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C as well.

7. Further the complainant has also made the allegations against the accused persons Gayatri Devi, Kunal @ Chintu and Navjot Bedi that they forcibly snatched the jewelery articles gifted to the complainant at the time of marriage and the description of the jewelery articles has been provided in the complaint of the complainant.

As the allegation of the complainant is that her jewelery articles were snatched rather than they were handed over by the complainant herself to the accused persons therefore it is not the case of entrustment U/s 406 IPC and instead of offences U/s 356/379 IPC are disclosed against the accused persons.
Gayatari Devi, Kunal and Navjot.

8. In so far as the accused persons Monty Tyagi @ Sunil Dutt Tyagi and Neelam Tyagi are concerned, no specific allegations have been made against them either in the complaint, statement U/s 161 Cr.P.C or the statement of the complainant U/s 164 Cr.P.C.
There is no sufficient material to frame charge against the accused persons )

Monty Tyagi @ Sunil Dutt Tyagi and Neelam Tyagi therefore, the accused persons,
Monty Tyagi @ Sunil Dutt Tyagi and Neelam Tyagi are discharged for the offences alleged.

9. From a perusal of the charge-sheet allegations and annexed documents inter-alia statement U/s 161 Cr.P.C. U/s Cr.P.C etc there is sufficient material on record to frame charge against the accused persons Gayatari Bedi, Kunal Bedi and Navjot Bedi U/s 498/356/379/34 IPC, against the accused person Udit Bedi @ Rinku and Meena Gogoi U/s 498A/34 IPC and against the accused persons Rajan Gogoi U/s 498/354/354 A IPC.

All the accused persons are discharged for the offence U/s 406.
4.

From the perusal of the reasons so given and the available record, I am of the opinion that the Ld.
Trial Court has not committed any illegality at all.
At this stage of consideration on charge, there is no requirement of evaluating the evidence or final probability of case projected by the prosecution.
It is sufficient if the order shows that Trial Court has applied its mind to the facts of the case and material on record.
Neither the defence of the accused persons nor the authenticity of claim of the prosecution is required to be decided at the stage of the charge.
The accused persons will certainly have sufficient opportunity to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses and also to lead evidence in defence.
Only after the completion of evidence, the Trial Court can form a final opinion in the case.
Every criminal trial is conducted only with a view to find the truth.
Such quest of truth should not be prohibited midway.
The prosecution should be allowed to establish its claim.

5. The arguments advanced by the Ld. Counsel for the revisionists and the averments made in the appeal touch the probable value of claim made by both the sides which cannot be done at the stage of charge.
I do not find any illegality in the order on charge as passed by the Ld. Trial Court.
6. It is however, interesting to note that in the revision petitions, the revisionists have not challenged the main order dated 30.07.2019 which was the basis of framing of charge on 22.08.2019.
The revisionists have only challenged the order dated 22.08.2019 and even in the prayer clause they have prayed only about setting aside of order dated 22.08.2019.
Unless the main order dated 30.07.2019 is challenged, the consequential order dated 22.08.2019 cannot be put to a challenge in revision petition.
This can be the other ground to say that the revision petitions cannot be allowed.

7. In view of the above discussion, I do not find any illegality in the order passed by the Ld. Trial Court and therefore, I dismiss all the three revision petitions mentioned in the first paragraph of this order.
8. A copy of this judgment along with Trial Court Record be sent to the Trial Court.
9. The Revision File be consigned to the Record Room after due compliance.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT TODAY ON THIS 18th DAY OF JANUARY, 2023 (RAKESH KUMAR SINGH) ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE (SOUTH)
SAKET COURTS : NEW DELHI )
